relation_checkpoint.selection_rule_applied: max validation top-1 (training_meta.val_acc); tie -> max val_macro_f1; tie -> lowest seed. Test metrics are not read.

object_reranked.objective: maximise POPE-adversarial F1 on the validation images; ties -> lower CHAIR_i; ties -> smaller L1 norm of the weights (prefer the simpler scorer); ties -> lexicographically smallest (w_obj, w_hall, w_rel). POPE F1 is used because it is symmetric: asserting an absent object costs a false positive and staying silent about a present one costs a false negative, so a caption cannot win by saying less - which CHAIR_i alone would reward.

notes: CHAIR/POPE ground truth: human Visual Genome annotations mapped to COCO-80; not exhaustive, so absolute hallucination rates are upper bounds for every arm.
Fallback images are scored with the baseline arm's caption (same prefix).
The threshold sweep reuses the grounded arm's relation captions and is exploratory; the primary result is the pre-declared threshold.

CLIPScore is reference-free image-text alignment (Hessel et al., 2021), not a reference-based caption quality metric; no reference captions exist for these images, so BLEU/CIDEr/SPICE are not reported.
